description:
Step 2 of fz-kdt.107's cure (cold review 2026-09-01).
runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities (types/mod.rs:2291) keeps a
FiniteSet<usize> of arities and discards sig.elems entirely, so
{:cont,X} and {:halt,Y} are ONE runtime question -- the root of
fz-kdt.104's original miscompile class and of probes/halt.fz. Add
per-position ATOM-TAG discrimination for fixed-arity tuples to
RuntimeTypePredicate: {:cont,_} vs {:halt,_} become different questions,
restoring the sound 'narrow test first costs precision, not meaning'
reading, dissolving the tuple class at the predicate rather than by
dropping (makes fz-kdt.118 belt-and-braces rather than sole defence).
Cost measured cheap in principle: emit_i64_membership/
emit_u64_membership already implement the per-value membership check
live for atom membership -- a new test SITE, not a new test kind; the
predicate is consumed by three backends, measure all three paths.
Corpus census note: this separates ZERO of the 17 in-corpus
indistinguishable groups (12 closure-identity + 5 list-element) -- its
value is the source-reachable tuple class (halt.fz), so the acceptance
fixture is halt.fz-shaped, not a corpus lens.
title: The runtime predicate cannot see a tuple's tag: per-position atom discrimination for fixed-arity tuples
